name: high-key-white-monolith
prompt: Every gang member wears a knitted balaclava covering the whole head, with no eye, nose or mouth holes; a large white ring is stitched round the face, and a red triangle sits high over the wearer's left eye (on the right of the picture, at about 2 o'clock); gloves on both hands, collars and cuffs closed, no skin showing anywhere. A tall portrait photograph of an endless white room with no corners: the floor curves up into the back wall in one smooth sweep, so there is no horizon line at all, only a soft field of white that fades to nothing at the edges. Exactly in the middle stands a towering block of stacked white office paper, squared off with knife-sharp edges like a minimalist plinth, rising past two thirds of the frame and dwarfing everything near it; the sheets show as faint fine lines along its sides. Fixed to the floor at its foot is a small plain card label reading "THE RULES" in neat black sans-serif capitals, the only lettering in the picture. Five gang members stand evenly spaced in a straight line a few paces in front of the block, bodies angled away from us towards it, chins lifted as they stare up its height, heads turned just enough that each mask's front shows in three-quarter view. Their knitted balaclavas are each a different loud colour: lemon yellow, cobalt blue, hot pink, emerald green and orange, every one carrying the white ring and red triangle; below the neck they wear ordinary present-day clothes in charcoal and black, a zipped hoodie, a puffer jacket, a bomber, plain trousers, black trainers, black gloves. The camera is set well back at chest height, perfectly level and square to the block, with the composition mirrored left to right and generous empty white above the stack. Lighting is bright, even and almost shadowless, as if the whole room glows, with only a faint grey contact shadow beneath each pair of feet and the block; whites are clean and slightly overexposed without washing out the masks. Palette: white and pale grey everywhere, black and charcoal clothing, and the only colour in the frame comes from the knitted masks and their small red triangles. Crisp, sharp, gallery-catalogue photography, realistic textures of wool and paper.
